results.summary: This is an analog computing tile that implements a chain of two EML cells, each computing exp(u) minus ln(v) in current mode using translinear NPN loops. The chain is configured through a 29-bit scan chain and biased from an on-chip PTAT core with a trimmed reference resistor. The design is built at the transistor level and includes a test cell, with only the final output observable through the analog pins. Testing requires a source-measure unit and attention to the slow PTAT start-up at cold corners.

results.summary: This project is a reconfigurable logic circuit built from identical rotatable tiles, each containing a NAND gate, a D flip-flop and a buffer. It is a port of the original ROTFPGA from Caravel to TinyTapeout, reduced to an 8x8 tile fabric with 8 inputs and 8 outputs. Configuration and reset use a scan chain, and the design was rewritten as hand-optimized gate-level Verilog. The author's silicon test report states that it works as expected.
